newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares seen cautious on budget debate.
newsitem.headline: India shares seen cautious on budget debate.

text.p: Indian shares are expected to tread cautiously with a bullish bias this week as market players watch a crucial debate on a pro-business budget unfold in parliament, dealers said at the weekend.
"There are some worries about whether or not the budget will be passed," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers.
But a price correction seen last week is likely to stoke investment buying, he said. "I think it will be a bullish week."

The parliament began on Friday a debate on the 1997/98 (April-March) budget presented by Finance Minister P Chidambaram on February 28 with the main opposition party saying the euphoria it had generated would be shortlived.
Chidambaram, interviewed by Reuters on Saturday, said he believed the budget would be passed by parliament.
"It is, in fact, a half budget," former prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee said, opening the debate for his rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Vajpayee was referring to a yawning oil subsidy deficit that Chidambaram did not take into account in the budget, otherwise hailed by business as a bold and innovative package.
"When the government effects the hike in the prices of petroleum products to tackle the deficit, the already thinning euphoria over the budget would totally vanish," he said.
Some constituents that form the 15-party coalition government have also criticised the budget as "pro-rich".
Political bickering on the main proposals outlined in the budget could lead to choppy trading, analysts said.
Chidambaram slashed corporate and personal taxes, raised foreign portfolio limits in local firms and allowed companies to buyback their shares.
Shares soared nearly 16 percent as players cheered the market-friendly budget which exceeded their expectations. It later fell on a correction.
The benchmark 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index lost 130.73 points, or 3.4 percent, to 3,745.31 last week.
Traders said they would also be watching a meeting between Chidambaram and the central bank on Monday.
The finance minister told Reuters he would seek ways to bring down interest rates and ensure adequate credit flows to industry.
Some analysts see buy opportunities in certain sectors.
"Funds are buyers in software, multinational, banking and refinery stocks," said Neeraj Batra, president at Hinduja Finance Ltd.
"I am advising people to take deliveries. The market should stage a small rally," Sequeira said.
